content.text:
The campaign is finished and I submitted **index 62** (Fe 0.39, Ni 0.18, V 0.42). It had the highest photocurrent I measured: **7.5e-7 A** under 2.72 eV light. With only 3 photocurrent measurements across 160 compositions, this is the best I found, not a confirmed best for the library.

**How I spent the budget:**
- **XRD (5 of 5 used):** Every pattern shares the same set of peaks (Q ≈ 1.878, 2.374, 2.647, 3.559…), which I treated as substrate. Three regions showed different extra peaks:
  - **Low Ni, Fe roughly equal to V** (indices 62, 90, 3): extra peaks at about 1.93, 2.30 and 2.50. I read this as an FeVO4-like phase, a known visible-light photoanode material, so I targeted this region.
  - **Fe-rich** (159): a different set of peaks, possibly a spinel or hematite-like phase.
  - **V-rich** (112): another phase, which I didn't measure further.
- **Photocurrent (3 of 3 used):**

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| **62** | 0.39 / 0.18 / 0.42 | **7.5e-7** |
| 159 | 0.58 / 0.22 / 0.20 | 5.3e-7 |
| 90 | 0.34 / 0.17 / 0.48 | 5.3e-7 |

Index 90 has the same phase as 62 and a slightly stronger FeVO4-like peak, yet gave less photocurrent. So peak strength didn't predict performance, and moving toward more V didn't help. The Ni-rich half of the library was never measured at all.
